notes:
**Manuscript v0.8.27 highlights:**

- Word Count says at the top of the window what a journal profile has locked
- A word limit set by the journal profile is shown as text
- The locked list of counted sections scrolls and expands
- A fully locked Word Count has one Close button
- The Word limit box has full-size step arrows
- Zoom now makes tables in the Catalog larger or smaller on screen
- A zoomed table says so
- One Zoom box, in percent, in the main window and the Catalog
- View → Reset Text Size is now Reset Zoom
- An export no longer stays in memory after it finishes
- Typing over a selection that ends with a footnote marker keeps every letter
- Rejecting a tracked deletion brings a footnote marker back live
- Undo and Redo keep footnotes correctly numbered
- Bold, italic and underline work in a footnote
- A footnote marker no longer brings a space with it
- The extra space after footnote markers already in a project is removed when the project opens
- Backspace over a footnote marker leaves your word space alone
- The Footnotes tab in the Catalog stays current
- The notices about footnotes say plainly what happened
- A subsection excluded from export stays out of the grant files
- Funder Readiness names every section that is in no attachment
- Footnotes in grant attachments cite in full under a note citation style
- Each grant attachment keeps the numbers the editor shows
- Grant attachments are never set below the funder's minimum font size
- Grant attachments follow the project's heading settings
- A funder profile that names no font gives the same attachments on every computer
- File → Export and Print use the funder's page in a grant
- Print uses the same page as File → Export PDF
- A grant project always recognizes its own submission package folder
- Exporting a grant no longer marks the project as changed
- The submission package reports every limit in the funder's own unit
- A grant package exported without a ZIP removes the ZIP of the previous export
- The Funder Profile window keeps every section's starter text
- Renaming a section title in a funder profile keeps the section you wrote
- A shipped funder profile you edit is kept as your own "(edited)" copy
- Saving or importing a funder profile under a name already in your library asks first
- The NSERC profile's margins stay at three-quarters of an inch
- A grant written in Word keeps its own sections when you choose a funder profile
- Export Grant Application describes the package it will write
- Funder Readiness says which attachments have nothing written yet
- Funder Readiness checks the PDFs you supply
- The grant status chip says what its count refers to
- A grant's reference list goes into its funder's bibliography attachment
- Exporting a grant checks the reference list first
- A grant's review draft comes back through Import Reviewed DOCX as a Word export does
- The review draft shows your pending tracked changes and comments
- The review draft uses the funder profile's line spacing
- Citations in the review draft follow your citation style
- Writing the review draft asks before replacing a file
- Footnotes and page numbers in a PDF use the body's font
- Footnotes in a grant attachment are no smaller than the funder allows
- Import Reviewed DOCX merges sentences that have a footnote when the file has no export record
- A kept sentence no longer holds back its whole paragraph
- An import that changes nothing in a section no longer counts it as merged
- Turning a reviewer's heading into a section keeps its footnotes
- No false "you have edited this section" notice for two footnotes side by side
- Undo takes back a whole column drag in one step
